# Hashtag corpus

Curated seed tags for this site's subject matter. The skill draws candidates from here, then you confirm each one in the LinkedIn composer before publishing.

**last_verified: 2026-07-31**

> Refresh when this is more than 90 days old. The niche tier decays fastest — new tags form around emerging topics within months, and cooled ones stop returning readers.

## How tiers work here

LinkedIn removed public hashtag follower counts in late 2024. **The tiers below are relative breadth and competition judgments, not measured follower counts.** No number in this file claims to be a follower count, because none can be.

| Tier | Means | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Broad | Enormous volume, enormous competition | Exactly 1 per post, for category placement |
| Mid | Real audience, still navigable | 2 per post — this is where the readers are |
| Niche | Small, specific, high intent | 2 per post, for precision and longer visibility |

## Language and stack tags

Small communities, very high relevance when the post genuinely concerns the stack. Use as a niche tag only when the stack is actually the subject.

`#Python` · `#TypeScript` · `#JavaScript` · `#Rust` · `#Go` · `#CSharp` · `#Kubernetes` · `#Docker`

## Responsible AI

**Niche** — `#ResponsibleAI` · `#AIEthics` · `#AIGovernance`

Strong in policy and enterprise circles. Only when the post genuinely engages the topic.

## Banned list

Screen every candidate against this. Drop matches without substituting a near-variant.

| Tag | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `#NFT` `#Metaverse` `#Web3` `#Crypto` | Hype cycles cooled; engagement fell sharply by 2026 |
| `#Success` `#Hustle` `#Grind` `#Motivation` `#Mindset` | Associated with motivational spam in content scoring; may suppress distribution |
| `#Like4Like` `#FollowForFollow` `#LinkedInFamily` | Engagement-bait patterns |
| `#Innovation` when the post is not about innovation | Not banned outright, but a frequent mismatch — the single most common misuse in this corpus |
| Any tag not matching the post's actual subject | Mismatch damages distribution more than the reach gain helps |

## Rotating starter sets

Keeping 3–4 themed sets and rotating whole sets beats picking tags from scratch each time. Each set below is a valid 5-tag 1-2-2.

**Set A — design and structure**

```text
#SoftwareEngineering #SoftwareArchitecture #CodeQuality #SystemDesign #TechnicalDebt
```

**Set B — AI-assisted engineering**

```text
#ArtificialIntelligence #GenerativeAI #DeveloperProductivity #AICodeAssistants #AgenticAI
```

**Set C — testing and correctness**

```text
#SoftwareEngineering #Testing #TDD #CodeQuality #TestAutomation
```

**Set D — craft and leadership**

```text
#Leadership #EngineeringCulture #EngineeringLeadership #SoftwareCraftsmanship #TechCareers
```

## Refreshing this file

1. Open the LinkedIn post composer and type `#` followed by each niche-tier tag. The composer surfaces what the platform currently indexes — the only live signal available.
2. Search the tag, filter to **Posts**, sort by **Recent**. No posts in the last month means the tag is functionally dead; remove it.
3. Note tags appearing repeatedly in high-performing posts from creators in the same subject area, and add them to the niche tier.
4. Move any tag whose competition has clearly grown up a tier.
5. Update `last_verified` at the top.
